raw_response.overlap_rationale: Both full texts are readable companion articles by Daniel M. Nzengya arising from the exact same May–June 2013 fieldwork project in three informal settlements in Kisumu, Kenya (Nyalenda A and Nyalenda B under KIWASCO's Delegated Management Model [DMM], compared against Manyatta B as a non-DMM control slum), conducted with the same three undergraduate research assistants and IRB approvals, and explicitly cross-referencing each other. The two papers primarily divide the study's respondent groups—Study B (2015) focuses on the supply side (interviews with N = 103 individual water-kiosk operators [47 Nyalenda A, 26 Nyalenda B, 30 Manyatta B; df = 2, 100] and N = 8 master-operator key informants), whereas Study A (2017/2018) focuses on the demand/user side (interviews with N = 294 adult water-kiosk customers sampled at those kiosks [109 Nyalenda A, 107 Nyalenda B, 78 Manyatta B; df = 2, 291] plus N = 46 microbiological water samples). However, the samples partially overlap rather than being completely disjoint: Study A Section 3.1 directly analyzes and reports kiosk-level observations and operator interview data from the N = 103 kiosk operator sample (queuing customers F(2, 100) = 3.63, containers F(2, 100) = 1.1, and operator-reported daily operating hours [11.6 h] and disruption hours [3.3 h]), and the 294 customers in Study A are nested within the same sampled KIWASCO kiosks evaluated in Study B on parallel outcomes (20-litre jerrican price and service disruption/reliability).
raw_response.study_a_sample_and_data: May–June 2013 fieldwork in Kisumu, Kenya comparing two DMM slums (Nyalenda A and Nyalenda B) with a non-DMM control slum (Manyatta B), using KIWASCO's list of individual water-kiosk providers as the sampling frame. Primary sample comprises N = 294 adult water-kiosk customers (109 Nyalenda A, 107 Nyalenda B, 78 Manyatta B; ANOVA df = 2, 291) interviewed at randomly sampled kiosks (text states 90 kiosks: 44 Nyalenda A, 28 Nyalenda B, 25 Manyatta B), supplemented by N = 46 water samples tested for total coliforms and E. coli (8 kiosks, 4 vendors, 12 wells/springs, 22 households) plus kiosk-level observations and operator interview responses on operating/disruption hours from the N = 103 kiosk sample (ANOVA df = 2, 100 in Section 3.1).
raw_response.study_b_sample_and_data: May–June 2013 fieldwork in the same three Kisumu slums (Nyalenda A and Nyalenda B with DMM vs Manyatta B control), using KIWASCO's list of individual water-kiosk operators as the sampling frame. Primary sample comprises face-to-face interviews and kiosk observations with N = 103 randomly sampled water-kiosk operators (47 Nyalenda A, 26 Nyalenda B, 30 Manyatta B; ANOVA df = 2, 100) plus in-depth key informant interviews with N = 8 master operators (representing all 5 group and 3 individual master operators in Nyalenda A and B).
